import json
URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robert-koch-institut/ARE-Konsultationsinzidenz/65ac2d278c06333808415795d65f0347c54be638/ARE-Konsultationsinzidenz.tsv"
R=1.0
base_tf=[
 {"filter":"datum.Bundesland==='Bundesweit' && datum.Altersgruppe==='00+'"},
 {"calculate":"toNumber(datum.ARE_Konsultationsinzidenz)","as":"v"},
 {"calculate":"toNumber(substring(datum.Kalenderwoche,0,4))","as":"isoYear"},
 {"calculate":"toNumber(substring(datum.Kalenderwoche,6,8))","as":"isoWeek"},
 {"calculate":"datetime(datum.isoYear,0,4,12) - ((day(datetime(datum.isoYear,0,4,12))+6)%7)*864e5 + (datum.isoWeek-1)*7*864e5","as":"date"},
 {"calculate":"(day(datetime(datum.isoYear,0,1))==4 || (day(datetime(datum.isoYear,0,1))==3 && ((datum.isoYear%4==0 && datum.isoYear%100!=0) || datum.isoYear%400==0))) ? 53 : 52","as":"nWeeks"},
 {"calculate":"2*PI*(datum.isoWeek-1)/datum.nWeeks","as":"theta"},
 {"joinaggregate":[{"op":"max","field":"v","as":"vmax"}]},
 {"calculate":"(floor(datum.vmax/1000)+1)*1000","as":"rmax"},
 {"calculate":"datum.v/datum.rmax*sin(datum.theta)","as":"cx"},
 {"calculate":"datum.v/datum.rmax*cos(datum.theta)","as":"cy"},
 {"calculate":"'W'+pad(datum.isoWeek,2)","as":"wk"}
]
peak_tf=[
 {"window":[{"op":"row_number","as":"rk"}],"groupby":["Saison"],"sort":[{"field":"v","order":"descending"}]},
 {"filter":"datum.rk==1"}
]
sc={"domain":[-1.12,1.12],"nice":False}
X={"field":"cx","type":"quantitative","scale":sc,"axis":None}
Y={"field":"cy","type":"quantitative","scale":sc,"axis":None}
color={"field":"isoYear","type":"ordinal","title":"ISO year","scale":{"scheme":"viridis"},"legend":{"columns":2,"symbolType":"stroke"}}
tt=[{"field":"Kalenderwoche","title":"ISO week"},{"field":"Saison","title":"Season"},{"field":"v","title":"ARE per 100,000","format":","}]
brushf={"filter":{"param":"brush"}}

circle={
 "width":560,"height":560,
 "title":{"text":"Cyclic view: one turn per ISO year (W1 at top, clockwise)","fontSize":13},
 "data":{"name":"are"},
 "layer":[
  # rings
  {"transform":[{"aggregate":[{"op":"max","field":"rmax","as":"rmax"}]},
     {"calculate":"sequence(1000,datum.rmax+1,1000)","as":"ring"},{"flatten":["ring"]},
     {"calculate":"sequence(0,73)","as":"k"},{"flatten":["k"]},
     {"calculate":"datum.ring/datum.rmax*sin(2*PI*datum.k/72)","as":"cx"},
     {"calculate":"datum.ring/datum.rmax*cos(2*PI*datum.k/72)","as":"cy"}],
   "mark":{"type":"line","color":"#ddd","strokeWidth":1,"interpolate":"linear"},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"detail":{"field":"ring"},"order":{"field":"k"}}},
  # ring labels
  {"transform":[{"aggregate":[{"op":"max","field":"rmax","as":"rmax"}]},
     {"calculate":"sequence(1000,datum.rmax+1,1000)","as":"ring"},{"flatten":["ring"]},
     {"calculate":"0.012","as":"cx"},{"calculate":"datum.ring/datum.rmax","as":"cy"}],
   "mark":{"type":"text","align":"left","baseline":"bottom","dy":-1,"fontSize":10,"color":"#777"},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"text":{"field":"ring","format":","}}},
  # spokes + week labels
  {"transform":[{"aggregate":[{"op":"count","as":"n"}]},
     {"calculate":"sequence(1,53,4)","as":"w"},{"flatten":["w"]},
     {"calculate":"2*PI*(datum.w-1)/52","as":"t"},
     {"calculate":"[0,1]","as":"e"},{"flatten":["e"]},
     {"calculate":"datum.e*sin(datum.t)","as":"cx"},{"calculate":"datum.e*cos(datum.t)","as":"cy"}],
   "mark":{"type":"line","color":"#eee","strokeWidth":1},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"detail":{"field":"w"},"order":{"field":"e"}}},
  {"transform":[{"aggregate":[{"op":"count","as":"n"}]},
     {"calculate":"sequence(1,53,4)","as":"w"},{"flatten":["w"]},
     {"calculate":"2*PI*(datum.w-1)/52","as":"t"},
     {"calculate":"1.06*sin(datum.t)","as":"cx"},{"calculate":"1.06*cos(datum.t)","as":"cy"},
     {"calculate":"'W'+datum.w","as":"lab"}],
   "mark":{"type":"text","fontSize":11,"color":"#444"},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"text":{"field":"lab"}}},
  # dimmed context lines
  {"mark":{"type":"line","strokeWidth":1,"opacity":0.12},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"detail":{"field":"isoYear"},"color":{"value":"#888"},"order":{"field":"isoWeek"}}},
  # highlighted lines (brush)
  {"transform":[brushf],
   "mark":{"type":"line","strokeWidth":1.6,"opacity":0.9},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"color":color,"order":{"field":"isoWeek"},"tooltip":tt}},
  # season peaks
  {"transform":peak_tf+[brushf],
   "mark":{"type":"point","filled":True,"size":110,"stroke":"black","strokeWidth":1.2,"shape":"diamond"},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"color":{"field":"isoYear","type":"ordinal","legend":None},"tooltip":[{"field":"Saison","title":"Season peak"}]+tt}},
  {"transform":peak_tf+[brushf],
   "mark":{"type":"text","fontSize":9,"dx":0,"dy":-10,"color":"#222"},
   "encoding":{"x":X,"y":Y,"text":{"field":"Saison"}}}
 ]
}

linear={
 "width":640,"height":330,
 "title":{"text":"Linear view: whole series (drag to select a time range)","fontSize":13},
 "data":{"name":"are"},
 "encoding":{"x":{"field":"date","type":"temporal","title":"Date (Monday of ISO week)","axis":{"format":"%Y","tickCount":{"interval":"year","step":1}}},
             "y":{"field":"v","type":"quantitative","title":"ARE consultations per 100,000 per week"}},
 "layer":[
  {"params":[{"name":"brush","select":{"type":"interval","encodings":["x"]}}],
   "mark":{"type":"line","strokeWidth":1.2,"color":"#4a4a4a"},
   "encoding":{"tooltip":tt}},
  {"transform":peak_tf,
   "mark":{"type":"point","filled":True,"size":70,"stroke":"black","strokeWidth":1,"shape":"diamond"},
   "encoding":{"color":{"field":"isoYear","type":"ordinal","legend":None},"tooltip":[{"field":"Saison","title":"Season peak"}]+tt}}
 ]
}

spec={
 "$schema":"https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
 "title":{"text":"Does the acute respiratory illness (ARE) peak arrive at the same time every year? Germany, 2012–2026",
   "subtitle":["Before 2020 every season peaked in ISO weeks 5–12 (Feb–Mar); the pandemic broke the rhythm (2021 peak in September, 2022/23 and 2023/24 in December),",
               "and 2024/25 and 2025/26 returned to February.  ◆ = highest week of each season (2026/27 is incomplete).  Radius = ARE consultations per 100,000 per week.",
               "Source: Robert Koch-Institut, ARE-Praxis-Sentinel (CC BY 4.0), all ages, Bundesweit."],
   "fontSize":17,"subtitleFontSize":12,"anchor":"start"},
 "datasets":{},
 "data":{"url":URL,"format":{"type":"tsv","parse":{"ARE_Konsultationsinzidenz":"number","Bundesland_ID":"number"}},"name":"are"},
 "transform":base_tf,
 "hconcat":[circle,linear],
 "resolve":{"scale":{"color":"shared"}},
 "config":{"view":{"stroke":None}}
}
del spec["datasets"]
json.dump(spec,open("spec.vl.json","w"),indent=1,ensure_ascii=False)
EOF

I've written `/work/spec.vl.json`. It renders with no errors or warnings. It shows a polar chart on the left and a time series with a brush on the right. I checked the link by rendering a test copy with a brush preset to mid‑2021 to mid‑2024: only those years stayed coloured in the circle and the colours didn't change. I then rendered the deliverable as-is.

**What the data shows:** every season before 2020 peaked in ISO weeks 5–12 (February to March). After the pandemic the timing moved: the 2020/21 peak came in week 39 (September 2021), and 2022/23 and 2023/24 both peaked in week 50 (December). 2024/25 and 2025/26 went back to February (weeks 7 and 6).

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - x/y computed from angle=2π(week-1)/weeksInIsoYear, W1 at top, clockwise; radius = value
  R2: done - one line per ISO year, viridis colour by year with legend
  R3: done - highest week per Saison (window row_number) marked with a diamond and season label
  R4: done - linear line chart 2012-W40 to 2026-W43 on a temporal axis (Monday of each ISO week)
  R5: done - x-interval brush in linear view filters the coloured lines/peaks in the circle; other weeks stay faint
  R6: done - week labels W1, W5, …, W49 around circle, ring values labelled, year axis, y title with unit; subtitle states radius unit
  R7: done - title plus caption sentence (subtitle) on the shift of peak timing after 2020
assumptions:
  - ISO-week dates are computed in the expression language (Monday of week, from Jan 4); 53-week years are found from Jan 1 weekday and leap year
  - If two weeks tie for a season's maximum, only one is marked
  - Ring spacing is 1000 and outer radius is max rounded up to 500; these are layout constants, not data values
  - The caption's numbers (weeks/months) were checked against the data; the caption text itself is static
limitations:
  - Season 2026/27 is incomplete (to 2026-W43); its "peak" is the maximum so far
  - Each ISO year is a separate line, so there is a gap between week 52/53 and week 1 of the next year
  - Peak labels overlap where several seasons peaked in similar weeks (Feb); the tooltip gives the exact values
  - The brush starts empty (everything highlighted); you drag on the linear view to select a range
```
